jobs.title: GIS Coordinator – Planning & Zoning
jobs.description:
Who We Are

The Town of Harrisburg is one of the fastest-growing communities in North Carolina and considered one of the top ten affluent zip codes in the surrounding region. While growth has been exponential over the past ten years, the Town has been able to maintain its tight knit community-based mindset and strategically foster a work culture where customer service excellence is our #1 priority.

What We Need

An employee in this class is responsible for the administration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Town's Geographic Information System (GIS), including enterprise geospatial databases, data integrity, spatial analysis, cartographic production, and GIS application support. Responsibilities include managing and maintaining geospatial datasets; developing maps, data visualizations, and analytical reports; conducting research and spatial analyses to support planning, infrastructure, and operational decision-making; and ensuring the accuracy, accessibility, and reliability of GIS information. The employee provides technical GIS support and expertise to Town departments not limited to Planning, Engineering, Public Works, Stormwater, Parks and Recreation, Code Enforcement, Administration, assists the public with GIS-related requests, and responds to inquiries from external agencies, consultants, and other organizations as appropriate. Work is performed under the general supervision of the Planning Director and is evaluated based on technical proficiency, accuracy, quality of work, effectiveness in meeting departmental objectives, and feedback from Town officials, staff, and the public.

Required Education And Experience

Graduation from a four-year college or university with a major coursework in Geography, Geospatial Science, Planning, Computer Science, Engineering, or a closely related field and at least 3 to 5 years of professional GIS experience, including data management, spatial analysis, and map production; or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Possession of a valid North Carolina driver's license.\

Preferred

Experience working in local government or supporting municipal operations, including planning, engineering, public works, utilities, parks and recreation, or other public sector environments. Familiarity with SQLite data format. GISP certification, Esri technical certifications, or other relevant GIS credentials preferred.

What We Offer

An excellent comprehensive benefits package and a desirable place to work where employees feel appreciated for their contributions.

The hiring range is $67,643 - $84,141 annually and starting salary will be dependent on qualifications and prior experience. Eligible for $2,500 sign-on bonus upon hire.

Please submit resume, employment application, references and salary requirements to either resumes@harrisburgnc.gov or at https://www.harrisburgnc.org/jobs.aspx.

Launch Your GIS Career with Pape-Dawson

Are you passionate about geospatial technology and eager to build your career with an industry-leading engineering and consulting firm? At Pape-Dawson, you'll have the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals on projects that help shape communities across the country. As a GIS Technician I, you'll gain hands-on experience with the latest GIS technologies while supporting impactful engineering, planning, environmental, and infrastructure projects.

Role

As a GIS Technician I, you'll support the development and maintenance of geospatial data, maps, and reporting products while working under the guidance of experienced GIS professionals. In this role, you will:

Create GIS data layers, maps, tables, reports, and other spatial deliverables using ESRI's ArcGIS suite and related applications.

Professional development, training, and career advancement opportunities
Collaborative, team-oriented culture with mentorship from experienced professionals
Opportunities to work on innovative, high-impact projects across multiple disciplines

If you're ready to build your GIS career with a company that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth, we'd love to hear from you.

Why STV?
You will join a collaborative team that is investing in the future infrastructure delivery—combining survey expertise, reality capture, automation, and digital tools to deliver better data, faster for our clients.

If you are a geospatial leader who enjoys mentoring teams, building strong client and project relationships, and turning complex field data into practical project intelligence, this role offers the platform to make a measurable impact across a growing Texas operation.

What You’ll Do

Manage and guide UAV/UAS, laser scanning, mobile mapping, LiDAR, GNSS, and reality capture efforts for transportation, utility, municipal, construction, and infrastructure projects.
Process, manage, and quality-check geospatial data using tools such as Trimble Business Center, Leica Cyclone, DJI Terra, Pix4D, Civil 3D, and related platforms.
Develop accurate digital deliverables, including point clouds, orthomosaics, terrain models, surface models, existing conditions models, utility mapping, and 3D reality capture datasets.

Support boundary, deed, easement, right-of-way, survey, utility, construction, and as-built deliverables in coordination with licensed survey professionals.
Integrate geospatial data into design and digital delivery workflows using Civil 3D, OpenRoads, ArcGIS, MicroStation, and related applications.
Help advance STV’s Better Data, Faster initiative by improving workflows, applying automation, and supporting the use of AI, digital twins, and reality capture technology.
Lead technical input for scopes, proposals, estimates, client discussions, standards, and best practices for geospatial and reality capture services.
Serve as a trusted technical and managerial resource for field teams, CAD staff, survey technicians, engineers, and multidisciplinary project teams while maintaining safe and compliant practices.

What You’ll Bring

10+ years of experience in surveying, geomatics, geospatial technology, reality capture, or a related field.
Hands-on experience with UAV/UAS, LiDAR, laser scanning, photogrammetry, GNSS, and geospatial data processing workflows.
Strong knowledge of survey principles, coordinate systems, control networks, field-to-finish workflows, and data quality standards.
Experience supporting transportation, municipal, utility, land development, construction, or infrastructure projects.
Proficiency with tools such as Trimble Business Center, Civil 3D, Microsoft Office, Leica Cyclone, Pix4D, DJI Terra, ArcGIS Pro, OpenRoads, MicroStation, Carlson Survey, or similar platforms.

Company Description

Job Description

***IMPORTANT NOTE: Candidate(s) selected for the Scientist (Water Ecology) position through this posting will be hired on a provisional basis. To be considered for permanent employment in this role, provisional employees will need to take and pass the next civil service examination for Scientist (Water Ecology) and obtain a list number issued by the NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services. Please be aware that employees who do not take and pass the exam may not be able to continue in the provisional position.***

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) enriches the environment and protects public health for all New Yorkers by providing 1.1 billion gallons of high quality drinking water, managing wastewater and stormwater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP's water supply system is comprised of 19 reservoirs and 3 controlled lakes throughout the system's 2,000 square mile watershed that extends 125 miles north and west of the City.

The Bureau of Wastewater Treatment (BWT) is responsible for the operation and maintenance of all facilities related to the treatment of sewage within the five boroughs of the City. This includes 14 wastewater treatment plants, sludge dewatering facilities, collections facilities (pumping stations, combined sewer overflow retention facilities, regulators, tide gates, etc.), wastewater laboratories and harbor vessels.

Under supervision, with some latitude for the exercise of independent initiative and judgment, the selected candidate will be responsible for participating in year round sampling in all weather conditions during Harbor Survey Cruises and field surveys for the Remote Monitoring Program; assisting in the production of annual reports and assisting with the development and review of additional sampling programs. Duties will include: On board processing of samples following strict SOPs; assist in the calibration and repair of instruments; schedule and perform routine maintenance on instruments and stations; assist the field supervisor with placement of monitoring locations; prepare graphics, maps, and/or text for Annual report; perform data analysis as requested; proofread and perform QA/QC for report production; develop new sampling initiatives as required; assists with memos/reports and other documents related to additional sampling; and lift and carry coolers weighing up to 50 pounds.

SCIENTIST (WATER ECOLOGY) - 21538

Qualifications

A masters degree from an accredited college or university in one of the following areas of study: environmental or chemical engineering, limnology, environmental science, marine science, geology, biology, earth science, chemistry, physics, or health science; or
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university with 24 semester credits in one or a combination of the areas of study described in ""1"" above, at least 12 of which must have been in one of these areas of study; and at least one year of satisfactory full time experience, which may not have been part of graduate or undergraduate course work, working in the field of water quality planning, management or

research or performing environmental laboratory analyses, and/or environmental field sampling of water; or

An associate degree from an accredited college or university including or supplemented by 24 semester credits in one or a combination of the areas of study described in "1" above, at least 12 of which must have been in one of these areas of study; and at least three years of satisfactory full time experience as described in "2" above.

Additional Requirements

To be assigned to Assignment Levels II or III, all candidates must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university as described in "2" above and must have one additional year of the experience described in "2" above for a total of two years of experience.

Special Note

A master's degree from an accredited college in one of the areas described in "1" above may be substituted for up to two years of the required experience.

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for an Environmental Engineer (Professional Engineer)
for our Columbus, Ohio office. We will also consider applicants for our Cincinnati, Dayton, Ohio; Cleveland, Ohio; Indianapolis, Indiana; Lexington and Louisville, Kentucky offices.

At WSP, you can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates different perspectives and innovative thinking. As part of our Earth & Environment team, you will collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry to help clients solve complex environmental challenges, protect natural resources, and build a more sustainable future. You'll have access to national expertise, global resources, and meaningful opportunities to grow your career while doing the work the world needs. With us, you can.

As an integral member of our Earth & Environment Team, you will actively participate in a variety of projects that support a growing organization focused on achieving client objectives and addressing their challenges. You will join a team of professionals dedicated to providing environmental consulting services.

At WSP, you'll find the culture, flexibility, and opportunities to build a career as unique as you. Our people are empowered to explore new challenges, collaborate across disciplines, and make a lasting impact on communities around the world. We foster an environment that is:

Open – We seek out different perspectives, ideas, and ways of working.
Curious – We nurture innovation and encourage new thinking.
Passionate – We take pride in delivering meaningful work that positively impacts society and the environment.
Adaptable – We embrace change and view it as an opportunity for growth and development.

Whether your goal is to deepen your technical expertise, lead complex projects, mentor future professionals, or expand your influence across the business, WSP offers the tools, resources, and support to help you grow. From mentorship and technical learning opportunities to leadership development and multidisciplinary collaboration, you'll be empowered to shape your own career path.

Key Tasks and Areas of Focus Assist in developing processes and infrastructure related to water supply, wastewater treatment, hazardous or solid waste disposal, air emission sources, and pollution control.
Work to preserve environmental quality of air, water, and land resources.
Generate accurate and concise reports and documentation detailing field conditions.
Assess and provide guidance regarding short- and long-term risks to ecological and human health.
Ensure that responsibilities are executed and maintained at a quality level that meets or exceeds industry standards.
Experience in environmental, health and safety compliance.
Support business development activities as part of your role within the team.

Your Impact

As a member of our Earth & Environment Team, you will collaborate closely with team members to provide strategic direction and support for existing client relationships. In the capacity of Project Engineer, you will be responsible for managing current and future projects, engaging with clients daily to establish and guide the strategic direction for project execution.
You will independently manage and execute projects to ensure compliance with established schedules. This role involves performing moderately complex technical tasks within broad work scopes, as well as planning, scheduling, conducting, and coordinating project work for large-scale assignments.
Your responsibilities include preparing technical proposals and reports, either in whole or in part, based on the size and complexity of each document. You will demonstrate competency across several areas, including engineering, field supervision, technical expertise, and task management. Additionally, you will motivate, train, and mentor junior staff assigned to your tasks or projects.
The position comprises approximately 80% office work and 20% field work, covering a variety of projects such as industrial, commercial, and State and Federal sites. You will be responsible for preparing technical reports and related documents and assisting with business development.
Further duties include preparing components of investigation and engineering reports, such as work summaries, data summaries, engineering calculations, summary tables, figures, engineering drawings and specifications, and report text. You will also conduct technical evaluations and provide recommendations as required.
As the primary point of contact for subcontractors, you will direct junior-level staff overseeing field activities, organize field work, assign tasks, and provide guidance to staff specialists in field task management. Your role also involves assisting in subcontractor procurement and overseeing field activities such as drilling (including DPT/Geoprobe, HSA, and Sonic), soil excavation, demolitions, and remediation system installations.
You will review contractor submittals, including equipment documentation, Work Plans, and QA/QC plans, and will be responsible for tracking payment applications, requests for information, change order requests, and general construction phase submittals. The role requires travel to project sites as needed, which may include overnight travel.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Master's degree in Environmental Engineering or equivalent discipline.
7–10 years of relevant experience.
Current Professional Engineer (PE) license or ability to obtain within six months of hire.
Strong computer and writing skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Ability to interact effectively with regulatory agencies, stakeholders, and clients.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond a typical work schedule.
Ability and willingness to travel to project sites as necessary.
Excellent time management and compliance tracking skills.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated initiative, attention to detail, and ability to work independently.
Proficiency with technical and business writing, office automation, and communication software.
Proficiency with discipline-specific design software and engineering tools.
Proven commitment to workplace safety and adherence to WSP health and safety policies.
Experience managing small to mid-size projects, including project scoping, budget tracking, and resource management.
Ability to plan and conduct inspections and investigations of facilities and structures.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to mentor junior staff while maintaining strict adherence to QA/QC procedures.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Experience managing small to mid-size projects.
40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120) with annual refresher preferred.
Basic First Aid and Adult CPR training desired.

The Office of Radiological Health (ORH) licenses and inspects more than 7,000 facilities using radioactive materials and x-ray producing equipment throughout New York City to ensure compliance with public health and safety regulations. Schedule and inspect facilities that use radiation-producing equipment throughout New York City for compliance with NYC Health Code and applicable State and Federal regulations.
Perform on-site tests of radiation-producing equipment installations.

Description

Chapman University invites applications for an Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science & Policy and Program Director in the Schmid College of Science and Technology starting August 2027. This is a full-time, tenured position that requires work to be performed in the State of California with specific in-person teaching responsibilities and required on-campus availability at Chapman's Orange campus.

Chapman University is a nationally ranked R2 institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California's most diverse and vibrant regions. Our faculty are academic leaders who excel in both research and teaching. Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at www.chapman.edu.

The Environmental Science & Policy Program is uniquely seated within two colleges at Chapman University: the Schmid College of Science and Technology and the Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges embody Chapman's mission of providing students with personalized educational experiences by fostering an outstanding community of teacher-scholars across a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs. Schmid College has a new 140,000 sq ft home, the Keck Center for Science and Engineering. More information about Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges is available at www.chapman.edu/science
and www.chapman.edu/wilkinson
, respectively.

The undergraduate-only serving Environmental Science & Policy Program is home to a diverse group of faculty with interdisciplinary specializations across the breadth of environmental sciences (ecology, engineering, hydrology, remote sensing) and environmental studies (anthropology, environmental justice, natural resource governance, political science, sociology). The program serves the interdisciplinary Environmental Science & Policy B.S. degree, the Environmental Science minor, and the Environmental Studies minor.

We seek candidates with an active research program in areas including but not limited to:

Environmental health
Environmental toxicology
Water, soil, and/or air quality
Environmental contaminants
Natural resource governance

We value candidates who can identify avenues for collaboration both within and outside of the institution.

Faculty Role Responsibilities

The successful candidate will teach lower- and upper-level courses that contribute to the major and minors within the Environmental Science & Policy Program, maintain an active research program, and advise/mentor undergraduate research students. Significant scholarship, including publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at relevant research conferences, and obtaining and managing extramural grants is an expectation of the position.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Teach lower- and upper-division Environmental Science & Policy courses, including core and elective courses. Current course descriptions are available at https://catalog.chapman.edu.
Continue a research program in interdisciplinary environmental sciences, including publishing papers and presenting work in this area at local and national conferences.
Actively contribute as an integral member of the Schmid College of Science and Technology in the ongoing development, implementation, and assessment of their academic and degree programs.
Perform service to the unit, college, university, profession, and wider community as expected of a tenured faculty member.

Program Director Responsibilities

The successful candidate will lead the Environmental Science & Policy faculty and degree program as Program Director for a minimum of three years in an at-will, compensated appointment separate from their faculty role.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Provide leadership, vision, and a voice for affiliated faculty, students, and degree programs.
Oversee program budget and advocate on behalf of the program for resource use.
Lead curriculum alignment and revisions, assessment reports, and course scheduling for the program.
Coordinate and participate in program and college events, including events for student recruitment and commencement, as appropriate.
Assign faculty to courses and hire appropriate part-time lecturers where needed.
Facilitate communication and collaboration between Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges pertaining to the support of this interdisciplinary program.

Qualifications

An earned Ph.D. in one of the environmental sciences (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science & Management) or related field by the start of employment from an accredited institution.
Earned tenure at the current institution of employment or equivalent.
A strong history of interdisciplinary environmental science research, including evidence of an independent, nationally recognized, externally funded research program.
Evidence of effective teaching at the undergraduate level, particularly in experiential learning courses, such as a senior capstone course, or upper division coursework.
Experience in curriculum development and learning outcome assessment.
Experience in leadership or administrative roles in academic service settings, such as college governance, curriculum, or assessment committees, ideally connected to interdisciplinary endeavors.

Application Instructions

Qualified Candidates Should Submit The Following Electronically Via Interfolio:

Cover letter detailing qualifications related to the position description.
Curriculum Vitae.
Statement of teaching philosophy that includes a brief description of past teaching experience, no more than two pages.
Research Statement that details current and future environmental science research, no more than two pages.
Statement of leadership philosophy that includes a brief description of administrative and leadership experiences as they relate to Program Director-level service, no more than one page.
Contact information for three professional references. Letters will be requested from short-listed candidates.

Inquiries may be directed to Richelle Tanner, Search Committee Chair, at schmidcollege@chapman.edu. Please use "Environmental Science & Policy Faculty Position" as the email subject line.

Chapman University invites applications for an Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science & Policy and Program Director in the Schmid College of Science and Technology starting August 2027. This is a full-time, tenured position that requires work to be performed in the State of California with specific in-person teaching responsibilities and required on-campus availability at Chapman's Orange campus.

Chapman University is a nationally ranked R2 institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California's most diverse and vibrant regions. Our faculty are academic leaders who excel in both research and teaching. Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at www.chapman.edu.

The Environmental Science & Policy Program is uniquely seated within two colleges at Chapman University: the Schmid College of Science and Technology and the Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges embody Chapman's mission of providing students with personalized educational experiences by fostering an outstanding community of teacher-scholars across a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs. Schmid College has a new 140,000 sq ft home, the Keck Center for Science and Engineering. More information about Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges is available at www.chapman.edu/science
and www.chapman.edu/wilkinson
, respectively.

The undergraduate-only serving Environmental Science & Policy Program is home to a diverse group of faculty with interdisciplinary specializations across the breadth of environmental sciences (ecology, engineering, hydrology, remote sensing) and environmental studies (anthropology, environmental justice, natural resource governance, political science, sociology). The program serves the interdisciplinary Environmental Science & Policy B.S. degree, the Environmental Science minor, and the Environmental Studies minor.

We seek candidates with an active research program in areas including but not limited to:

Environmental health
Environmental toxicology
Water, soil, and/or air quality
Environmental contaminants
Natural resource governance

We value candidates who can identify avenues for collaboration both within and outside of the institution.

Faculty Role Responsibilities

The successful candidate will teach lower- and upper-level courses that contribute to the major and minors within the Environmental Science & Policy Program, maintain an active research program, and advise/mentor undergraduate research students. Significant scholarship, including publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at relevant research conferences, and obtaining and managing extramural grants is an expectation of the position.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Teach lower- and upper-division Environmental Science & Policy courses, including core and elective courses. Current course descriptions are available at https://catalog.chapman.edu.
Continue a research program in interdisciplinary environmental sciences, including publishing papers and presenting work in this area at local and national conferences.
Actively contribute as an integral member of the Schmid College of Science and Technology in the ongoing development, implementation, and assessment of their academic and degree programs.
Perform service to the unit, college, university, profession, and wider community as expected of a tenured faculty member.

Program Director Responsibilities

The successful candidate will lead the Environmental Science & Policy faculty and degree program as Program Director for a minimum of three years in an at-will, compensated appointment separate from their faculty role.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Provide leadership, vision, and a voice for affiliated faculty, students, and degree programs.
Oversee program budget and advocate on behalf of the program for resource use.
Lead curriculum alignment and revisions, assessment reports, and course scheduling for the program.
Coordinate and participate in program and college events, including events for student recruitment and commencement, as appropriate.
Assign faculty to courses and hire appropriate part-time lecturers where needed.
Facilitate communication and collaboration between Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges pertaining to the support of this interdisciplinary program.

Qualifications

An earned Ph.D. in one of the environmental sciences (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science & Management) or related field by the start of employment from an accredited institution.
Earned tenure at the current institution of employment or equivalent.
A strong history of interdisciplinary environmental science research, including evidence of an independent, nationally recognized, externally funded research program.
Evidence of effective teaching at the undergraduate level, particularly in experiential learning courses, such as a senior capstone course, or upper division coursework.
Experience in curriculum development and learning outcome assessment.
Experience in leadership or administrative roles in academic service settings, such as college governance, curriculum, or assessment committees, ideally connected to interdisciplinary endeavors.

Cover letter detailing qualifications related to the position description.

Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

products. Ability to be on call or work off hours as needed

14001 & 45001, 37001 helpful)

Superior communications, interpersonal, and organizational skills required
